i want to add a few things to close some dead ends of the puzzle:
1) the solution of x2sh does not give us decentraland coordinates. decentraland was a hint to find a second door. i presume that the solution of decentraland  'HASHTHETEXT' is maybe the solution of the 3.2.2 aes, because i see no way to find this 2nd door by accident.
the reason? it's just imposible if you realize the timeline:
19. dec 2018 - funding of the decentraland eth-address with decentraland-mana
13. Apr 2019 - funding of the btc address with 5 btc
13-20 Apr 2019 - release of the puzzle (20th was the first discussion on reddit)
28 May 2019 - funding of the decentraland address with eth, outgoing transaction of mana, acquisition of the estate
14. Jan 2020 'roses are white but often red... Hush hush' - hint
Feb 2020 opening of decentraland (don't know the exact date)
20 Feb 2020 - release of the hint with the decentraland picture (hashthetext)
11 May 2020 - halving, splitting of the price

So here's this. I know by the way some are talking there are a some who are already focusing on it but let's just put it out there:

Ciao Bella O.

There's 2 angles I'm considering on this.

1 is the song O Bella Ciao, in Italian. It has been mentioned. But the line is backwards, in the worst gear. The first phases used the first lines of a song chorus as a password. The first words of O Bella Ciao are "One morning I woke up". Sounds pretty matrixy to me. Maybe backwards either character by character or in reverse order of words.

The other possibility is a reference to ciphers. I was looking at the chaocipher and Bellasso cipher but couldn't reconcile them with a base 9 alphabet.

Ciao Bella O is a major hint. Jrk is practically screaming it at us with all of his Ciao messages. We should be focusing on this.

I’ve been looking into the prime function recently and for binary we need 7/8 bits to make 2 corresponding alphabets which makes sense and for hexadecimal we need 2 characters to make a corresponding byte or 8 bits which still represents 1 byte of data or 8 bits
What’s the difference between the 2 of them if they’re achieving the same thing?
Binary consumes more space while hexadecimal consumes less
And decimal is just an awkward representation because unlike hexadecimal that has a base 16 and it compresses more data more than the base10 system 
We can relate the three interchangeably but we all know that without the decimal, there’s no prime numbers. So everything has to be represented as base10 before any operation can be carried out when it comes to encoding and decoding with prime functions
You don’t need base10 for binary operations neither do you need base10 for hexadecimal operations
But you need it for prime operations 
You can’t do anything without base10 in prime operations

text:
I will leave this group today as I found some unpleasant facts about this puzzle. 

I encourage everyone to think twice before trying to find solutions. The puzzle is badly designed. There are serious flaws and this comes from someone who has worked with _hush hush_ data all his life. 

Just two examples.  I have  found many more. 

1. When OP_data (part of the puzzle) was added in TX for the 'causality' brain wallet, it was done on the compressed side - 1Jqq37KkZEt4F3Dt6qXdtyiMEFBBdawbkJ – The puzzle makers did not even check to see that the uncompressed address was already created in 2013. I guess they found out after the puzzle was made public [this alone adds unplanned and unnecessary confusion and for me it shows bad design]

2.  You can read all the public OP_data directly on the blockchain instead of going through whatever phase and whatever ciphers [this was also unplanned] How? Just use a blockchain parser and search for 47534d472e (ASCI for their website). Sample at:   blockchain [dot] info/block/000000000000000000078fbc77e0c5e2b10ade8880a265c140e6e36d29b2da29?format=hex ] --- this is only for a single block but of course it's all there...

3.  Moreover, the January 2020 hint was announced as THE LAST hint, see chat history.  And yet, others were posted after. This can only prove that they realized this puzzle cannot be solved

them frequently interfering in the solving process. My sincere advice to them: please, do not provide any more clues to these poor people.  These clues [which are different puzzles altogether!] cannot help unexperienced solvers with their thinking process. And the users who think they have understood the hints just because they got onto the next phase they will be in for quite a surprise. 

4.  I am not interested in the actual prize. It will be unethical for me to actually claim it and it might have quite some negative consequences on me if I do so [and the word gets out]. I wanted to say nothing, but I can see so many are messaging me [please don’t] and struggling and it’s all because of a bad design not because the puzzle is hard - in popular layman terms. I was here to send a professional warning to all those spending too much time on this – it's a nice try but it was not built well and you will waste more time than you think because the construct is flawed. 

Just ask yourself: what if there were no clues at all? None. Just the puzzle. For how long people would still be stuck? Years perhaps. Why? Because you NEED clues and that is bad design.  

Do something better with your time. Have fun, read and work hard. Be kind to others, it will pay off. 

As for this puzzle, even if you get to a so called final stage trust me, you will hit the biggest wall of all and you will be quite disappointed. 
 
Adios! Exiting the channel soon …👋🏻

messages.text:
forget mnemonics. at least not in the way described in BIP-39 with later usage of BIP32 and BIP44.
mnemonics do map words to binary for sure (one word produces 11 bits [2^11=2048]).
But in BIP39 this input is used to create a seed after some hashing rounds, the seed is then later used to create deterministic wallets as specified in BIP32 and BIP44.
As the prices address is a vanity address there is no way 'back' to a BIP39 mnemonic. Yes - you could represent any private key with a mnemonic and throw away the last 4 bits (which is a checksum), but that's not specified as any standard to represent a private key.

messages.text:
tltr: in ~1/256 of the cases a random key does not throw a decryption error in openssl's aes implementation, thus a false positive.
it expects a padding  with bytes corresponding to the padded-length to the 16 byte boundary.
eg:. 
a3 d3 42 f2   3f 03 03 03 
or
a3 d3 42 f2   3f 2f a1 01
if the decryption ends with '01' or '02 02' (and so on) there will be no error.

messages.text:
To represent the letter "a" (lowercase) in octal, you would first need to convert it to its ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) value. The ASCII value for "a" is 97 in decimal notation. To convert this decimal value to octal, you can use mathematical conversion methods.

Here's how you can convert the decimal value 97 to octal:

Divide 97 by 8:

97 ÷ 8 = 12 with a remainder of 1.
Divide the quotient (12) by 8 again:

12 ÷ 8 = 1 with a remainder of 4.
Continue this process until the quotient becomes 0:

1 ÷ 8 = 0 with a remainder of 1.
Now, you can read the remainders from bottom to top to get the octal representation. In this case, it is 141. So, the octal representation of the letter "a" is 141.

messages.text:
Chaotic Image Encryption Based on the Spatial Domain
In image encryption, the term spatial domain refers to the image itself. Since digital images are composed of a large number of pixels, spatial-domain-based image encryption means directly operating on these pixels. This can include shuffling image pixels or blocks, changing the value or position of pixels in the original image, and other similar operations. At present, most chaotic image-encryption algorithms employ spatial-domain encryption, while others use frequency-domain encryption

Prime numbers can be used in various cryptographic ciphers to enhance security or provide mathematical properties that make encryption and decryption more robust. Here are a few examples:

1. RSA Encryption: The RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) algorithm is a widely used asymmetric encryption scheme that relies on the mathematical properties of prime numbers. In RSA, the security of the encryption is based on the difficulty of factoring large composite numbers into their prime factors.

2. Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange: The Diffie-Hellman key exchange protocol allows two parties to securely establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel. It utilizes prime numbers in the context of modular exponentiation to derive the shared key.

3. ElGamal Encryption: The ElGamal encryption system is another asymmetric cryptographic scheme that uses prime numbers. It relies on the properties of modular exponentiation and the discrete logarithm problem in finite fields to provide confidentiality.

4. DSA (Digital Signature Algorithm): DSA is a widely used digital signature scheme that incorporates the use of prime numbers. It relies on the mathematical properties of prime numbers in the context of modular arithmetic.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.image as mpimg
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the image
img = mpimg.imread('add.png')

# Convert the image to grayscale if it's RGB
if len(img.shape) == 3:
    img = np.mean(img, axis=2)

# Perform 2D Fourier transform
fourier_transform = np.fft.fft2(img)
magnitude_spectrum = np.fft.fftshift(np.log(1 + np.abs(fourier_transform)))

# Normalize the magnitude spectrum to the range 0-1
magnitude_spectrum_normalized = (magnitude_spectrum + np.min(magnitude_spectrum)) / (np.max(magnitude_spectrum) - np.min(magnitude_spectrum))

# Save the normalized magnitude spectrum as a new image
mpimg.imsave('magnitude_spectrum.png', magnitude_spectrum_normalized, cmap='viridis')

print('Normalized magnitude spectrum image has been saved as magnitude_spectrum.png')

messages.text:
Everybody here that has an idea, any idea, if willing to share it then plz do.... This puzzle has been going for years now, and not to put down any methods tried or suggested by anyone here except one and one only....

A method can always be done in many ways, so it is possible that a certain path will get us thru this current roadblock in the puzzle... I have many ideas and come up with more all the time, I share what i got for anyone to decide for themselves if worth checking out as well.... We dont have enough people sharing openly here and it sucks to be honest because new ideas are what is truly needed at this moment....

I dont hate (not worth the time or effort) but I do get annoyed with so many people telling others whats right or wrong way to solve this puzzle.... If anyone knew whats up, we all be working something else cause the prize  would have been had already, right??? 

So with full respect to all intellects and IQ's here, until you personally pull the prize, dont push your way of solving like its the truth and shut down others when you dont know what your talking about yourselves... (apply this statement to all who say "focus here and forget all else")

I dont know shit but ive learned alot doing this and other puzzles, and the best thing in all of it is trading ideas and methods with people that think different than me... I owe alot of what i now know to a few truly creative and experienced here as well as a few idiot savants that dont even know when they say something brilliant until showing them what they just helped accomplish even if by accident....

—— By the way I write alot, its just me, just a heads up ——

Even if you have the same ideas of what to do now or next that 100 people have said, share it still, because you might have a certain twist to your way of doing the same thing thats been tried, but yours is the way that finally works

dbbib and faed are now basically the de facto religion for gsmg puzzle solvers stuck at the farthest publicly known stage of completion....
not bad considering all they had to go thru to get there, i got mad respect for the skillsets needed to accomplish this....
Not to put down or throw shade on anybody and seriously i mean that, but im just curious as to how many know that all this bad ass puzzle solving was done almost/but basically as far back as when the puzzle came out...
It was longer than that of course but i took some time off the actual timeline taking into account the typo "givetit" that had so many stuck for an artificially long time and how fast after "give it" was given as the correction that so many blasted forward at a speed that Jrk felt the need to post comments on...
Im sure that not one but a few people are past this place most of us are stuck at, but even those few havent finished yet, which got me wondering just whats next....
All that being said, my main point here is that a good chunk of people that are dedicated to solving puzzles around the globe are all hitting this thing and judging by publicly made posts as well as a few private group posts, it really does look like nobody is going to solve this thing without another hint from Jrk, a lucky decrypt happens by accident, or a true mastermind hits this with a thought process equal to an alien mindset... 
So many talented individuals have been at this for so long that somebody you would think just by the odds alone would have solved this already, right???

So, once again, im not telling anyone what to do or how to do it with this puzzle cause i havent solved yet either...
What i am trying to do is to get people to change the way they think, because the collective of humanity as we know it today basically all (99.98%) has the same mindset/patterns/problem solving skillsets/and creative thinking processes worldwide..... Im not talking about peoples intellects on this either because that doesnt really come into play except when you know what to apply your knowledge to... Im talking about your mindset and ways of thinking about things... A genius and a dumbass are both equals many times and ways on this part...

Change your thinking..... 
Change your priorities....
Shift your focus.....

Why even after pointing out that there are currently unfound/unsolved/100% valid hints from Jrk himself (that even he hinted more than once), why are these all completely ignored or shied away from??? Seriously, they dont even get mentioned as a possible clue to solve dbbib or faed as if mention/mixing of these diff parts of the puzzle is an abomination of a thought...

Did you really read all i have posted to this point, mad respect for your dedication and patience,

Based on reactions and things that Jrk has said in the past and in predictions so far true (embedded in the puzzle before the puzzle was started), f#$k the white rabbit, how about follow_this_logic_instead?

Jrk inserted into the source codes of the puzzle that it was impossible to solve the puzzle (this will be true until we change our mindsets)

Jrk stated specifically about another door being hidden and most importantly after it wasnt found (in a short period of time), he posted again showing his surprise at NOBODY finding this other door...

(edit add-on): 
                            If one part is impossible in creators mind (why cant we let this go for a sec?)
                              when we could be hitting the part that he is surprised nobody found yet!!!
A=easy
B=hard «—(stubborn can be stuck here, but stupid is to do this without giving "A" a few chances as well)

People, myself included, have asked if that door hint was still a thing (It is by the way because nobody has bragged about it/shared it publicly or even with Jrk who would then update the public of events), anyway, people would ask about it only to go back to dbbib and faed immediately after...

What is so wrong with looking for other things that are known to have meanings (even if yet not understood), are 100% real (Jrk hinted them, didnt he?), and im assuming but feel safe doing so that these things will have to be figured out anyway at some point, so why not now???

At least with the hints we have a hint, unlike dbbib and faed where we have only opinions and guesses...
At least the hints are newish and different, since the puzzle has only been 2 strings for a few years now....
If it makes anyone feel better, we are not giving up on anything or quitting because its still the same puzzle we are working on...

I have a biased mind myself even though i pride myself in being more open minded and out of the box with my thinking than most (most people i know, not most people), but my mindset isnt creative enough yet to crack this thing, but i will not stop trying...

My apologies for the novel, but its just how i am, and for those of you that skipped to the end of this post;
just to prove i could have kept it short;

in summary: 
Drop Dbbib and Faed (not completely of course, just for now "put that pipe down")
Pick up a diff trail here using hints that for some reason are akin to talking about "Fight Club" or the name "Voldemort" (psst, its ok, a new path wont hurt you)
Dont give up, just do differently!
(see, could have made short if i wanted)
Good luck everyone!!!

text:
based on the fact that pretty much nobody has made any progress in multiple years, I think it’s about time for a holiday hint? At the least answer a couple questions for all of us that really wouldn’t be giving too much of anything away. 

1) can u confirm that the aes blob in salphaseion should decrypt to plain text? 2) are the hints that you’ve given for the puzzle in general, or specifically for the salphaseion phase? 3) I know there are multiple doors and ways to get the private key, but are there multiple private keys? You said you would be able to tell how someone solved it when it gets solved, so that means there has to be more than a single private key throughout the puzzle? 4) has there been a decision made on whether the 2.5 btc from the first halving will be made into another puzzle, or as a second solution to this puzzle? 

I really think we deserve answers to these questions, as answering them doesn’t really give anything away but could prevent a lot of people from literally wasting time if they misinterpreted your previous hints. For example we don’t even know if the primes have anything to do with salphaseion or if that’s a general hint for the puzzle, same goes for yellow and blue, & yin yang. Someone could spend months trying to figure out something with prime for salephaseion when it may not even have anything to do with that part of the puzzle. 

In previous phases of the puzzle there was at least some sort of direction given, but in salphaseion there is absolutely nothing to indicate what steps should be taken. I’ve spent almost six months on this and haven’t made any progress at all. 

I’m sure there are a lot of people in here that really could use the prize money and I don’t think it will ever be solved given the current state of things. Both of my grandparents passed away this year, and left my mom in a huge amount of debt from their medical bills, and with how much my mom has done for me I really pray that I could make some breakthrough to be able to help her and take that burden off her shoulders… it’s hard enough when you lose both of your parents especially the way she did with both of them passing away within a week of each other. And like I said I’m sure there are other people too who really desperately would benefit from the prize money, and it’s really unfortunate that as it looks now, nobody will end up getting it. And when you factor in that in a few months it will be halved, and then you account for taxes, what originally was a substantial prize ends up being less than the yearly wage of 95% of people in the us. And I’m sure there are a lot of people who have spent at least a year if not more on this puzzle. 

Anyway I’m sure I speak for everybody when I say I think it’s time for another hint, and hopefully one that would help people actually make some progress. I really hope this puzzle will at least be solved before the halving, bc if not it will just be really disappointing I think for all of us who have put so much time in trying to solve the puzzle. If nothing else, at the very least, please answer the questions I asked, I would really greatly appreciate that.

Also keep in mind, you created the puzzle, so giving a hint that may be obvious to you is not so obvious to everybody else. You have a bias because you already know all the answers.
